resources.string: Your PC wants to see the screen
Tap to share it. Android asks every time.
Tap to share it; Android asks every time. To use the phone from the PC too, turn on Fenpo in Accessibility.
The screen is on your PC
Lets your PC tap, swipe and type on this phone while you share its screen with Fenpo. It does nothing at other times.
Control your phone from the PC

Fenpo uses Android’s AccessibilityService API (accessibility service) so that, while you share this phone’s screen with your PC, the taps, swipes and typing you make on the PC happen on the phone. It finds the field you are typing into on the screen for that.
It works only while you are sharing the screen. It does not read or keep your screen for anything else, and sends nothing to anyone but your own PC.
Next, turn on “Fenpo: control from the PC” in Accessibility. You can turn it off there at any time.
